issues.legal_issue: Specification of individual shares in a decree does not, by itself, sever the joint-family status between members of the same branch.
material_facts: A partition suit brought by members of some branches of a joint family resulted in a preliminary decree specifying shares, including the shares of members within another branch.
The decree directed that the estate be divided into three allotments corresponding to branches, rather than separate allotments for every member.
The member whose share was specified was a minor represented by his uncle, and the record disclosed no unequivocal intention by the uncle or the minor to separate from one another.
issues.conclusion: The specification of shares did not sever the joint-family status between the members of the branch.
issues.legal_principle: Under Mitakshara Hindu law, partition requires an unequivocal intention to sever, expressed through conduct or agreement; mere ascertainment of shares is not enough, and severance between some family members does not create a presumption of severance between the others. Whether other members have severed is a question of fact assessed from all the circumstances. The Court relied on Palani Ammal v. Muthuvenkatacharla Moniagar & Ors.

rule.if: hindu_joint_family_partition_dispute and decree_specified_member_shares and allotments_were_directed_by_branch and not unequivocal_intention_between_branch_members

predicates.hindu_joint_family_partition_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether members of a Hindu joint family have partitioned their interests.
predicates.decree_specified_member_shares: A decree stated the shares of individual family members.
predicates.allotments_were_directed_by_branch: The decree directed separate allotments for branches rather than separate allotments for every member.
predicates.unequivocal_intention_between_branch_mem: The members of the branch expressed an unequivocal intention to separate from one another.

issues.definition: When a family partition decree specifies individual shares but directs allotments by branch and the branch members have not unequivocally intended to separate, their joint status is not severed merely by that specification.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory bar on claims concerning court-auction purchases does not apply when the claimant asserts that the property belongs to the joint family because it was acquired with joint-family funds in another person's name.
material_facts: The claimant sought a share in properties said to belong to the joint family, including properties purchased at court auctions in the name of a relative.
The concurrent findings were that family members acquired the properties with the aid of joint-family funds.
The claimant did not allege that the court-auction purchaser bought the properties on the claimant's behalf or on behalf of someone through whom the claimant claimed.
issues.conclusion: The claim was not barred by section 66(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 66(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a suit alleging that a certified court-auction purchaser bought property on behalf of the plaintiff or someone through whom the plaintiff claims. The provision restricts the court's jurisdiction to give effect to real rather than nominal title and must be strictly construed. A claim that property belongs to a joint family because it was bought with joint-family funds in another person's name does not fall within its terms. The Court relied on Addanki Venkatasubbaiah v. Chilakamerthi Kotaiah and distinguished its application of section 66(2).

rule.if: suit_claims_interest_in_court_auction_property and claimant_asserts_joint_family_ownership and purchase_used_joint_family_funds and not purchase_alleged_to_be_on_claimant_behalf

predicates.suit_claims_interest_in_court_auction_pr: A claimant brings a suit asserting an interest in property bought at a court auction.
predicates.claimant_asserts_joint_family_ownership: The claimant says the property belongs to the joint family.
predicates.purchase_used_joint_family_funds: The property was acquired using joint-family funds.
predicates.purchase_alleged_to_be_on_claimant_behal: The claimant alleges that the certified purchaser bought the property on the claimant's behalf or on behalf of someone through whom the claimant claims.

issues.definition: A claim to joint-family ownership based on the use of joint-family funds is not barred when the claimant does not allege that the auction purchase was made on the claimant's behalf or on behalf of a person through whom the claimant claims.

issues.legal_issue: A party need not formally plead that opposing evidence is fabricated or interpolated in order to challenge its reliability at trial.
material_facts: A party relied on a recital in a certified copy of a preliminary decree to support its case that the family had separated.
Other certified copies of the decree did not contain the recital, and the trial court found it unreliable as an interpolation.
The opposing party argued that the challenge to the recital should have been pleaded.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the reliability of the recital could be raised without a formal pleading that it was fabricated or interpolated.
issues.legal_principle: The Code of Civil Procedure does not require a party to amend its pleading whenever it contends that evidence relied on by the opposing party is unreliable. Reliability of evidence supporting a party's case may be challenged at trial without separately pleading that contention.

predicates.civil_trial_disputes_evidentiary_reliabi: A civil trial must determine whether evidence relied on by a party is reliable.
predicates.party_challenges_opponent_evidence: A party challenges the reliability of evidence put forward by the opposing party.
predicates.no_formal_fabrication_pleading: The challenging party has not formally pleaded that the evidence was fabricated or interpolated.

issues.definition: A party may challenge opposing evidence as unreliable at trial even without a formal pleading alleging fabrication or interpolation.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court that agrees with the trial court's assessment of the evidence need not restate the evidence or repeat the trial court's reasons.
material_facts: The trial court considered the evidence and found that the parties had not severed their joint-family status.
The appellate court generally approved the trial court's reasons without separately reappraising and restating the evidence.
The appellate court's agreement with the trial court's evidentiary view was challenged.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court's general agreement with the trial court's reasons was sufficient.
issues.legal_principle: When an appellate court agrees with the trial court's view of the evidence, it is ordinarily sufficient to express general agreement with the trial court's reasons; it need not restate the evidence or reiterate those reasons.

predicates.appeal_from_trial_court_evidentiary_find: An appeal concerns a trial court's finding based on evidence.
predicates.appellate_court_agrees_with_trial_court_: The appellate court agrees with the trial court's view of the evidence.

issues.definition: When an appellate court agrees with a trial court's evidentiary conclusion, it may state its general agreement with the trial court's reasons without repeating the evidence or those reasons.

issues.legal_issue: A claim for rendition of accounts is not extinguished by the death of the party claiming the account or the party required to render it.
material_facts: The decree directed an account of dealings with family property.
Two defendants who had been involved in managing the property died while the proceedings were pending.
The issue was whether their deaths prevented an account from being ordered against their estates.
issues.conclusion: The claim for an account survived the deaths, and the liability to account could continue against the estates.
issues.legal_principle: A claim for rendition of accounts is not a personal claim and is not extinguished by the death of either party. The maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona has limited application to certain personal actions ex delicto and does not apply to an action for accounts concerning property received or managed.

predicates.accounting_claim_in_civil_proceeding: A civil proceeding includes a claim for rendition of accounts.
predicates.party_claiming_or_owing_account_dies: A party entitled to an account or a party required to render one dies during the proceedings.
predicates.account_relates_to_property_received_or_: The account concerns property received or managed by the party required to account.

issues.definition: A claim for an account concerning property received or managed remains enforceable against the estate when either the claimant or the person required to account dies.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant's receipt of income from some family property does not release the family members managing the estate from accounting for their dealings after the claim for partition.
material_facts: The claimant had received income from some of the family property and possessed some portion of it.
Other family members had managed the family estate.

The claimant sought accounts from the time the parties had separated in estate and mess and residence, and the decree required accounts from the relevant demand for partition rather than for earlier dealings.
issues.conclusion: The claimant's receipt of income from some property did not absolve the managers from rendering accounts for their dealings after the demand for partition; the claimant's possession was to be considered in adjusting the account.
issues.legal_principle: A co-sharer’s possession of some family property or receipt of income from it does not by itself absolve those managing the family estate from accounting for their dealings after the claimant's separation and demand for partition. The value or income received by the claimant is considered in the final adjustment of the account, and past dealings are not included where the claim is limited to the period after separation.

rule.if: partition_and_accounting_proceeding and claimant_received_income_from_some_family_property and others_managed_family_estate and account_claim_is_for_post_demand_dealings

predicates.partition_and_accounting_proceeding: The proceeding seeks partition of family property and an account of its management.
predicates.claimant_received_income_from_some_famil: The claimant possessed some family property or received income from it.
predicates.others_managed_family_estate: Other family members managed the family estate.
predicates.account_claim_is_for_post_demand_dealing: The account sought concerns dealings after the claimant's separation and demand for partition.

issues.definition: When a claimant received income from some family property but others managed the estate, that receipt does not prevent an account of the managers' dealings after the demand for partition.
